proposal.reactor_type: PFA coil tubular reactor with in-line static micromixer, submerged in a thermostated oil/heat-transfer bath
proposal.tubing_material: PFA (main coil); Hastelloy C-276 fittings and mixer body for concentrated HNO3 contact zones
proposal.residence_time_basis: Total reactor coil volume (30 mL) divided by combined flow rate (2.0 mL/min) = 15 min nominal residence time at reaction temperature/pressure

streams.contents: Aniline derivative (assumed protected/stabilized against oxidation, e.g. as acetanilide or sulfonate-protected amine; free aniline is highly oxidation-prone under neat HNO3 and is not recommended)
streams.solvent: Glacial acetic acid (chosen as inert, HNO3-miscible carrier; batch protocol did not specify solvent explicitly, so acetic acid is assumed as the 'industrial batch solvent')

streams.contents: Fuming nitric acid (~21 M, ~90-98% w/w), serving simultaneously as nitrating reagent and Brønsted acid catalyst per batch description
streams.solvent: Neat (no additional solvent; excess HNO3 itself acts as reaction medium)

proposal.mixer_type: PTFE/PEEK T-mixer (0.4 mL internal volume) feeding into a SiC or PTFE static mixer chip before the main coil
proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Substrate stream is dosed into the excess nitric acid stream (not vice versa) to maintain a locally high NO2+ concentration, favor rapid electrophilic attack, and minimize contact time of free amine with dilute acid, which could otherwise promote oxidative decomposition/tar formation. Immediate high-shear mixing suppresses hot-spot formation from the strongly exothermic nitration.
pre_reactor_steps: Pre-cool nitric acid stream to 0-5 C before mixing to offset heat of mixing and reduce risk of thermal runaway upon contact with substrate stream
Filter/degas substrate solution to remove particulates that could cause channel blockage
Inert-gas (N2) blanket on both feed reservoirs to prevent moisture ingress and control off-gassing of NOx
post_reactor_steps: In-line quench into a stirred vessel of cold aqueous NaHCO3/ice (3-5x reactor volume) immediately after the BPR to neutralize excess HNO3 and halt reaction
Phase separation (organic dinitro product vs. aqueous acid) via liquid-liquid separator
Off-gas scrubber (aqueous NaOH trap) downstream of BPR to capture any NOx released upon depressurization
In-line FTIR or UV monitoring for reaction completion/dinitro selectivity
proposal.chemistry_notes: Batch process ran at 60 C for 4 h with HNO3 as both nitrating agent and acid catalyst, giving 89% dinitrated product. In flow, superior heat/mass transfer allows intensification: higher effective temperature (80 C) with drastically shorter residence time (~15 min total) while maintaining safety via small reactor holdup. Dinitration proceeds via sequential mono- then di-substitution; the first nitration is fast and highly exothermic (~-150 kJ/mol), the second slower and more temperature-dependent, so a two-stage reactor design is proposed (see stage_parameters). Elevated temperature and pressure (BPR) keep the reaction mixture liquid and suppress NOx off-gassing/cavitation in the tubing. Corrosion-resistant materials are mandatory given concentrated/fuming HNO3 at 80 C; standard stainless steel is unsuitable long-term.

stage_1_mononitration.purpose: Fast, controlled mono-nitration under moderate temperature to avoid runaway before full mixing is achieved

stage_2_dinitration.purpose: Slower second nitration requiring elevated temperature and longer residence for full conversion to dinitro product

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Batch used 4 h; flow intensification via improved heat/mass transfer typically reduces nitration residence times to minutes-scale, consistent with literature precedent for aromatic nitrations in flow.
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: Raised from 60 C (batch) to 80 C to compensate for shorter residence time while remaining below HNO3 boiling/decomposition onset under back-pressure.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: 0.5 M substrate assumed as a practical, pumpable concentration for a solid aniline derivative in acetic acid; not specified in batch protocol.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: 10 bar back-pressure selected to suppress NOx bubble formation and maintain single liquid phase at 80 C, standard practice in continuous nitration processes.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: PFA/Hastelloy chosen for compatibility with concentrated/fuming nitric acid; standard steel or PTFE alone insufficiassistant for long-term concentrated HNO3 exposure at elevated T.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: Sized to deliver ~15 min total residence at 2 mL/min combined flow, split across two thermal zones for staged mono/di-nitration control.
reasoning_per_field.mixer_type: High-shear low-volume mixer chosen to rapidly homogenize immiscible/reactive streams and minimize local hot spots given high exothermicity.

literature_analogies: Bogdan, A. R.; Jamison, T. F. et al., continuous-flow nitration of aromatics with fuming HNO3 in PFA reactors, demonstrating residence times of minutes vs. hours in batch.
Ducry, L.; Roberge, D. M. Org. Process Res. Dev. - continuous nitration of aromatic substrates showing improved safety and selectivity via microreactor heat transfer.
Industrial continuous nitroaromatic (e.g., DNT/TNT precursor) processes using staged temperature zones to control mono- vs di-nitration selectivity.
safety_flags: Highly exothermic nitration reaction - runaway risk if flow stops or cooling fails; automated interlocks (flow/temperature sensors triggering emergency quench) required.
Fuming/concentrated HNO3 is a strong oxidizer and corrosive; use of compatible wetted materials only (PFA, Hastelloy); avoid stainless steel above dilute HNO3 concentrations.
NOx gas evolution possible during reaction and upon depressurization; requires closed system with vented scrubber, not to be opened without proper ventilation.
Possible oxidative side reactions/tar formation with free (unprotected) aniline in strong HNO3; substrate should be protected (e.g., acylated) or process re-verified for the specific derivative.

Small reactor holdup volume (30 mL total) intentionally limits worst-case thermal excursion compared to batch reactor, but pressure relief and containment (blast shield) still recommended given oxidizer/organic combination.
This is a conceptual/derived design; the batch protocol did not specify solvent, exact acid strength, or safety data (e.g., DSC/ARC), all of which should be experimentally verified before scale-up.
